entities.name: Crinagoras of Mytilene
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Crinagoras of Mytilene (c. 70 BCE–after 11 CE) was a Greek epigrammatist from Lesbos who became a court poet in Augustan Rome. Of aristocratic Mytilenean background, he took part in embassies to Julius Caesar and Augustus on behalf of his city and settled into the cultural orbit of the imperial household, addressing epigrams to Augustus, Tiberius, and other notables. His surviving poems, preserved mainly in the Greek Anthology, treat gifts, imperial occasions, personal grief, and polished compliments in the concise elegiac style of Hellenistic epigram.

Crinagoras illustrates how Greek literary talent was absorbed into the patronage networks of early Imperial Rome: a provincial notable who converted embassy access into lasting poetic proximity to power. His work documents the bilingual cultural world of the Augustan elite and the continued prestige of Greek verse beside Latin poetry. For historians of Lesbos and of Augustan court culture, he is a rare named bridge between eastern civic politics and Roman imperial ceremony.
